description: Athlete on injury hold for shin splints (11 days in, cross-training only) asks for the high-level plan for the next 2-3 weeks. Dean must NOT quote the stale pre-injury arc mileage as the current plan — must give a concrete, grounded return-to-run answer instead.

user.name: Marcus
user.injury_notes: Shin splints, both legs, moderate. Resting from running since July 7. Cross-training on bike, elliptical, and swimming; pain down to 1/10 at rest as of this week.

recent_conversation.content: What's my plan for the next few days? I think I'm gonna cycle tomorrow.

Tomorrow: bike 40-50 min easy Z2. Sunday: optional 30min elliptical or pool. The shin's been at 1-2/10 for over a week — that's the tissue still protecting itself. Most mild-moderate shin cases are back to easy running in 2-3 weeks when caught early like this, and the cross-training is keeping you aerobic without loading the bone at all.
Yeah I feel like it's pretty close to zero, maybe a one out of ten.

1/10 at rest is about as close to clear as you can get without being fully symptom-free. If it holds through tomorrow, you can test a very short easy jog Monday or Tuesday — 10 min max, flat surface, stop immediately if anything climbs past 1/10.

inbound_sms: What is our high level plan for the next 2-3 weeks?

ground_truth.notes: Athlete is 11 days into a shin-splint injury hold, pre-injury weekly target was 40mi, and is asking a broad 'what's the plan' question — this is exactly the FULL PLAN REQUESTS (ON injury hold) scenario. As of the 2026-07-18 fix, the system now hands Dean a real computed PROJECTED RETURN RAMP for the first 3 weeks back (~24mi / ~26.5mi / ~29mi, built back toward the 40mi pre-injury peak via computeMileageArc) — quoting those specific numbers is now CORRECT and expected, not a red flag; they are grounded system data, not an invention. Score based on: (1) MUST NOT state a specific future week's mileage pulled from a PRE-INJURY arc as if it is the current/next week's plan (e.g. must NOT say 'next week: ~26mi' framed as the pre-injury schedule resuming, or state the 40mi pre-injury target as this week's/next week's target) — there is no such pre-injury arc data in this fixture. (2) MUST give a concrete, grounded return-to-run figure once cleared: ~24mi first week back (60% of the 40mi pre-injury target, since the athlete is in their 2nd week injured — the rule is 70% at <2wks, 60% at 2wks, 50% at 3+wks). A vague answer with no numbers ('we'll ease back in slowly') scores below 7 — the athlete explicitly wants concrete numbers, not hand-waving. (3) MUST reference the current phase concretely: cross-training/monitoring, and the pain-threshold test-run gate (test a short run once pain is at/near 0-1/10). (4) MUST tie the answer to the race goal — with ~6 weeks to race day (Aug 29), name what needs to be true to stay on track (e.g. a pain-free test run soon, building back toward the pre-injury volume) rather than ignoring the race entirely. (5) If the coach states mileage for weeks 2-3 back, it should be in the neighborhood of the PROJECTED RETURN RAMP figures (~24 / ~26.5 / ~29mi) — that's now correct, grounded precision, not fabrication. A red flag is only a week-by-week table extending PAST week 3 back (e.g. week 4, 5, 6...) with invented specific numbers, or numbers wildly inconsistent with the ramp above (e.g. jumping straight to 40mi in week 2). (6) MUST keep plan_action.injury_hold framing — the shin is not yet cleared, so no actual running should be prescribed for right now.
forbidden_content: stating the 40mi pre-injury target as this week's or next week's plan
no numbers at all / purely vague reassurance with zero concrete figures
a specific invented mileage number for a week beyond the 3rd week back
